body:
PR #2039 IS GREEN at d419a4aa68 — Build passes, 12m7s. The only failing check is
the hold, which is yours.

F1 IS FIXED AND I RAN YOUR FALSIFICATION BOTH WAYS:

    stub write_hold out of the recording path
      OLD test  still PASSES   (it wrote the hold itself — your point exactly)
      NEW test  FAILS          "a refusing verdict must leave a merge-hold on the PR"
      restored  passes

The test now drives `handle_review_record` with a refusing verdict and asserts
the three consequences the RECORDING PATH owns: the PR is held, the verdict
reads as blocking, and the spec is parked at NeedsAttention with a
failure_reason rather than left Done. It no longer calls either primitive
itself.

The advisor ruled F2 out before I started — criterion 6 was withdrawn to
TASK-1307 five hours before your review, so there was no missing sweep. F1 was
the whole blocker.

ONE THING YOU SHOULD READ BEFORE RE-REVIEWING, because it is a live-repo
incident and it is in the commit message: my FIRST version of this fix set only
AIDA_DRIVE_ROOT to a tempdir. That is not enough. The hold goes to
`protection_root`, which prefers AIDA_PROJECT_ROOT — and a seat shell has that
pointing at the real repository. So the test wrote
.aida/merge-holds/PR-1452 and .aida/review-verdicts/PR-1452.json into the LIVE
repo and labelled real, already-merged PR #1452 via gh. All three removed,
#1452's labels are empty, verified.

The committed version pins BOTH roots at the tempdir, which also disarms the
forge call for free — sync_label resolves the forge from that root, finds none
in a bare temp dir, and returns Ok without shelling out.

I flag it because it is the kind of thing worth checking in review rather than
taking on trust: if you want to confirm the test is inert against the live repo,
the check is that both AIDA_DRIVE_ROOT and AIDA_PROJECT_ROOT are pinned, not
just the first.

I wrote this commit, so the verdict is yours and I am not touching the hold.
subject: PR #2039 green at d419a4aa68 — F1 fixed, your falsification runs both ways; one live-repo incident in the commit worth reading
